heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles eSUN ePA-CF effectively right out of the box thanks to its standard hardened steel nozzle and enclosed chamber, topping out at a safe print speed of 131 mm/s governed by an 11 mm³/s volumetric limit. As a carbon-fiber filled polyamide, strict filament drying and high bed temperatures inside a fully sealed chamber are mandatory to prevent warping and rough surface finishes.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with PVP glue stick or liquid adhesive release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap the Max Volumetric Speed at 11 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent underextrusion during high-speed passes.
Set the Part Cooling Fan to 0% base speed with a maximum of 20% on short layer times (<15s) to ensure layer adhesion without delamination.
Enable Wipe While Retracting (2.0 mm) and Retract on Layer Change to minimize CF nozzle oozing and seam zits.
Adjust Pressure Advance to roughly 0.035 to 0.042 (run OrcaSlicer PA Line calibration) to eliminate corner bulging from carbon-fiber slurry friction.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and rough fuzzy outer perimeters
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: eSUN ePA-CF absorbs ambient moisture within hours, boiling off in the nozzle and creating microscopic steam explosions.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool at 70°C to 80°C for at least 8 to 12 hours in an active dehydrator or the X1C chamber dry cycle before printing from a dry box.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Part warping and lifting at bed corners
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: High crystallization shrinkage of polyamide combined with thermal draft or insufficient bed temperature.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Set bed temperature to 85°C, close the front glass door and top glass lid entirely, and apply a thin, uniform coat of PVP glue stick.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clicking and under-extrusion at infill transitions
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Carbon fiber agglomerates creating backpressure beyond the stock hotend melt rate when exceeding 11 mm³/s flow.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Raise nozzle temperature from 270°C to 280°C and limit infill speeds to match the 131 mm/s maximum linear print ceiling.

faq.question: Can I feed eSUN ePA-CF through the Bambu Lab AMS?
faq.answer: Yes, but prolonged use will wear the AMS plastic funnels and internal PTFE tubing due to the abrasive carbon fibers; ensure the spool itself is not warped cardboard.

faq.question: Does the stock 0.4mm nozzle on the X1C clog with ePA-CF?
faq.answer: The X1C includes a hardened steel 0.4mm nozzle which resists abrasion, but for extensive continuous production, a 0.6mm hardened nozzle virtually eliminates CF clogs.

faq.question: Why is a glue stick required on the Textured PEI plate?
faq.answer: Polyamide bonds aggressively to PEI and can tear the coating upon removal; the glue stick acts as an essential release interface and uniform thermal barrier.

faq.question: Should the auxiliary chamber fan be kept on or turned off?
faq.answer: Turn the auxiliary fan completely off (0%) in OrcaSlicer to prevent cold air drafts that trigger instantaneous layer separation and severe warping.
